title: Americans on several prescriptions at once
unit: Percent of people who used prescription medicines in the past 30 days, age-adjusted
context: A quarter of Americans now take three or more prescription medicines at once, double the share in the early 1990s.
ask: Are more people ill, or are more conditions now treated with medicine?

series.label: One or more
series.about: Americans of all ages who took at least one prescription medicine in the 30 days before the survey's health check.

series.label: Three or more
series.about: Americans who took three or more prescription medicines in the past 30 days: a common measure of how many medicines people combine.

series.label: Five or more
series.about: Americans who took five or more prescription medicines in the past 30 days, often called polypharmacy, which raises the risk of interactions.

numbers.text: on three or more prescriptions, 1988-1994 to 8/2021-8/2023.

caption: United States, all ages, from the national health and nutrition survey's medicine check. Survey periods run several years each.

sources.publisher: CDC / National Center for Health Statistics
